sentences.zh: 但我也明白，这反映在我们所看到的单独监禁中的自杀人数上，

sentences.en: confinement compared to the general prison population.
There is a very close relationship between solitary confinement and mental illness.
sentences.zh: 单独监禁与精神疾病之间存在着非常密切的关系。

sentences.en: One way to understand that is that in the 1970s and early 80s when mental institutions closed
sentences.zh: 理解这一点的一种方式是，在20世纪70年代和80年代初，当精神病院关闭时，

sentences.en: was the same time that mass incarceration and rates of incarceration were increasing across
sentences.zh: 正是大规模监禁和监禁率在美国各地增加的时期。
这意味着一些患有精神疾病的人不出所料地最终进入了监狱。

sentences.en: And that meant that some mentally ill people unsurprisingly ended up in prisons.
sentences.zh: 我提出的论点之一是，当这些人进入监狱时，他们往往

sentences.en: And one of the arguments I make is that as those people ended up in prison, they tended
to be put into solitary confinement.

sentences.zh: 是普通监狱人口的两倍甚至更高，这是一种解释。

sentences.en: be twice as high as in the general prison population or even higher.
sentences.zh: 而且隔离中的精神疾病发病率可能很高。

sentences.zh: 而且通常存在一个真正的先有鸡还是先有蛋的问题，你知道，一个人被送去隔离

sentences.en: And often there's a real chicken and egg problem of, you know, did a person get sent to isolation

各州已经试图限制这种情况。

sentences.en: And states have tried to limit that.
sentences.zh: 还是人们在隔离中患上了精神疾病？

sentences.zh: 我们大多数人永远不会看到超级监狱的内部。

sentences.zh: 但我们经常在流行文化中看到对单独监禁场景的描述。

sentences.en: But we often do see scenes of solitary confinement described in pop culture.
sentences.zh: 其中一个例子是电视剧《女子监狱》。

We have a bit of tape.
sentences.zh: 角色派珀被关进了一个安全住房单元，开始与她通过牢房栅栏听到的声音说话。

sentences.en: The character Piper is put into a security housing unit and starts speaking to a voice
she hears through the grate of her cell.
How long have you been down here?

sentences.zh: 他们一直开着灯，所以你失去了所有的时间感。

sentences.en: They keep the lights on so you lose all sense in time.

sentences.zh: 这已经不再是一个人了。

sentences.en: It ain't not a person no more.
sentences.zh: 你开始看到根本不存在的东西。

sentences.en: You start to see a **** that ain't there.

sentences.zh: 他们把你关在这里直到把你摧毁。

sentences.en: They keep you here until they break you.
sentences.zh: 卡拉米特，我想知道那种对单独监禁真实生活的描述有多准确。

sentences.en: I feel like I'm going to throw up.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为你听到与派珀交谈的那个虚无的声音在很多层面上都是准确的。

sentences.en: Karamit, I'm wondering how accurate that description is of what life's actually like in solitary confinement.
sentences.zh: 那个声音的情感表达是平淡的，而囚犯描述了听到声音，即幻觉。

sentences.en: I do think that the disembodied voice that you hear talking to Piper is accurate on a number of levels.
sentences.zh: 这是隔离非常常见的副作用。

sentences.en: The voice is kind of flattened in affect, and the prisoner was describing hearing voices, hallucinations.
sentences.zh: 人们谈论时间，谈论他们感知时间的方式发生了变化，因为没有办法标记时间。

sentences.en: That's a very common side effect of isolation.
sentences.zh: 人们谈论它的方式和那个囚犯说的一模一样。

sentences.en: And people talk about time, the way they perceive time changing because there is no way to mark time.
sentences.zh: 并不是说它感觉很漫长。

sentences.en: People talk about it exactly as that prisoner said.
sentences.zh: 只是它几乎是无止境的，日子可能会以一种奇怪的、反直觉的方式飞逝，因为没有任何东西可以标记一天或一周。

sentences.en: It's not that it even feels long.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，它是准确的。

sentences.en: It's just that it's almost endless, that days can kind of, in a weird, counterintuitive way, fly by because there's nothing marking anything about a day or a week.
sentences.zh: 我想花点时间谈谈你在研究这个问题上的角色。

sentences.en: So in that sense, it's accurate.
sentences.zh: 一方面，你是一位花时间研究这个问题的研究员，但正如你自己所说，你也是一名监狱权利倡导者。

sentences.en: I want to spend a moment talking about your own role in looking at this.
sentences.zh: 你曾在人权观察组织和其他组织担任活动家。

sentences.en: On the one hand, you're a researcher who has spent time studying the question, but as you yourself have said, you're also a prison rights advocate.
sentences.zh: 当你对单独监禁有非常明确的强烈观点时，你如何保持对该主题的分析能力？

sentences.en: You've been an activist at Human Rights Watch and other organizations.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我采访卡尔·拉尔森时，他说，好吧，你是个伯克利的自由派。

sentences.en: How do you preserve your ability to be analytical about the subject while you also have what are very clearly strong views about solitary confinement?
sentences.zh: 所以他让我做一些背景阅读，证明我是认真的，我会听他的。

sentences.en: You know, when I went to interview Carl Larson, he said, well, you're a Berkeley liberal.
sentences.zh: 所以我实际上认为在做这项工作的过程中，

sentences.en: So he asked me to do some background reading and prove that I was serious and I would listen to him.
sentences.zh: 我变得更加开放，并因与监狱官员进行如此直接和广泛的交谈而受到倡导者的批评。

sentences.en: And so I actually think in the process of doing this work,
sentences.zh: 所以我经历了一段有趣的尝试，试图在这个过程的广泛观点中保持对话的开放。

sentences.en: I have become more open-minded and been criticized by advocates for talking so directly and so extensively to prison officials.
sentences.zh: 我认为通过这种方式，我至少能够尝试整合这些不同的观点，并理清人们所持的论点和立场。

sentences.en: And so I've had the interesting experience of trying to keep the conversation open across a really broad spectrum of perspectives on this process.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为，在改革中，监狱官员必须走进这些机构，日复一日地与这些囚犯接触。

sentences.en: And I think in that way, I've been able to try to at least incorporate these different perspectives and tease apart the arguments and the positions people are coming from.
sentences.zh: 他们也需要成为改革对话的一部分。

sentences.en: And I do think that in reform, prison officials have to walk into these institutions and engage with these prisoners day in and day out.
sentences.zh: 通过这个过程，你知道，令人惊讶的是，尽管我基本上是从另一方来的，如果你想从立场的角度来考虑的话，我已经开始理解那个视角了。

sentences.en: And they also need to be part of the reform conversation.
sentences.zh: 卡拉米特，单独监禁中的人说他们怀念什么？

sentences.en: And through this process, you know, surprisingly, even though I came basically from the other side, if you want to think of it in terms of sides, I've come to see that perspective.
sentences.zh: 你怀念的那些我们其他人可能不会想到的事情是什么？

sentences.en: Karamit, what sorts of things do people in solitary confinement say they miss?
sentences.zh: 人们谈论多年或几十年没见过月亮，以及他们有多怀念这一点。

sentences.en: What are the kind of things that you miss that the rest of us might not think about?
sentences.zh: 然后人们谈论怀念纯粹的人类接触。

sentences.en: So people talk about not having seen the moon in years or decades and how much they miss that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在书中讲了一个故事，关于一个囚犯，他的牢房门和隔壁囚犯的牢房门被意外地同时打开了。

sentences.en: And then people talk about missing just pure human touch.
sentences.zh: 他们是敌对的帮派成员，但他们一直在交谈，通过牢房墙壁大喊大叫。

sentences.en: And, you know, I tell a story in the book about a prisoner who his cell door and the cell door of the prisoner next to him were accidentally opened at the same time.
And they were rival gang members, but they had been talking to each other, shouting through the through the cell walls.
sentences.zh: 他们只是伸出手抓住对方，紧紧握住，因为他们俩已经很久没有得到过那样的温柔的人类接触了。

sentences.en: And when the cell doors opened,
they just reached around and grabbed each other's hands and held on because it had been so long since either of them had had a gentle human touch like that.
sentences.zh: 囚犯通常每天独自待在牢房里22或23个小时。
你发现，在心理上真正应对这种情况的唯一方法可能就是坚持一系列非常、非常僵化的常规。

sentences.en: Prisoners often stay alone in their cells for 22 or 23 hours a day.
And you found that perhaps the only way to actually manage this psychologically is to stick to a series of very, very rigid routines.
sentences.zh: 我在这项研究中能够采访到的、以了解他们经历的囚犯往往是那些幸存下来的囚犯。
所以他们确实发展出了各种各样的应对机制。

sentences.en: The prisoners who I was able to interview in this research to understand their experiences tended to be the prisoners who survived.
sentences.zh: 我反复听到的一种机制是，他们会在早上第一件事，也就是早上5点醒来，然后做数千次重复的练习，

sentences.en: And so they did develop all kinds of coping mechanisMs.
sentences.zh: 通常是囚犯们所说的波比跳。

sentences.en: And one of the ones I heard about again and again was that they would wake up, you know, first thing in the morning, 5 a.m., and they would do thousands of repetitive exercises,
sentences.zh: 也就是开合跳、俯卧撑和仰卧起坐的组合。
你知道，早上确实要做几千次来开始他们的一天。

sentences.en: So a combination of jumping jacks, push-ups and sit-ups.
sentences.zh: 然后打扫牢房，写信，处理法律案件。

sentences.en: And, you know, literally a few thousand in the morning to start out their day.
sentences.zh: 通常在这些单元里，如果囚犯遵守规则，并且有家人寄钱进来，他们可以买电视或收音机。

sentences.en: And then clean their cells, write letters, work on legal cases.
sentences.zh: 而养成这些常规的囚犯谈到他们会真正限制听媒体的时间。

sentences.en: And in general in these units, if prisoners are following the rules and they have money being sent in from family, they can buy either a TV or a radio.
sentences.zh: 所以可能每天只听一两个小时，或者看他们喜欢的特别节目，这样他们就能在一天中自觉地让自己的身体和思想都保持忙碌。

sentences.en: And prisoners who develop these routines talk about really limiting the time they spent listening to media.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，囚犯们谈到在出狱后很难放弃这些常规，

sentences.en: So maybe only an hour a day or two hours a day or a special show they like to watch so that they were keeping both their bodies and their minds really busy consciously over the course of a day.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然会在每天早上5点起床时做那几千次波比跳，

sentences.en: And interestingly, prisoners talk about having trouble letting go of these routines once they got out of prison,
sentences.zh: 而且他们对居住的8乘10牢房中一切事物的控制能力也很难放弃，他们可以保持，你知道，

sentences.en: that they would still do those thousands of burpees every morning at 5 a.m.
sentences.zh: 一个囚犯向我描述他如何能保持牙膏盖子完美清洁。

sentences.en: when they got up, and that their ability to control everything in their space in that 8 by 10 cell they live in is also hard to let go of, that they could keep, you know,
sentences.zh: 当他出狱后有室友时，他无法再控制牙膏盖子的事实让他感到非常困难。

sentences.en: a prisoner described to me how he could keep the cap of his toothpaste perfectly clean.
sentences.zh: 所以这让你感觉到生存是多么激烈，以及这些应对机制在之后会持续多久。

sentences.en: And it was really hard when he had a roommate when he got out of prison, the fact that he couldn't control the cap of the toothpaste anymore.
sentences.zh: 卡拉米特，你在书中谈到囚犯尝试各种不同的事情，不仅是为了保持身体和心理活跃，还要表达情感，

sentences.en: So it kind of gives you a sense of how intense it is to survive and then how long those coping mechanisms linger afterwards.
sentences.zh: 试图找到做艺术活动的方法。

sentences.en: You talk in the book, Karamed, about inmates trying a number of different things to not just be physically active and mentally active, but emotionally expressive,
to try and find ways to do artistic things.
sentences.zh: 囚犯确实在努力寻找表达自己的方式。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that for a moment?
sentences.zh: 有时是变得非常精通法律并进行诉讼，但通常是自学绘画，有时是自学说一门新语言，

sentences.en: Prisoners do struggle to find ways to express themselves.
Sometimes that's becoming really good at the law and litigating cases, but very often it's teaching themselves to draw, sometimes teaching themselves to speak a new language,
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的故事之一是一个囚犯告诉我的，他在隔离室待了几个月，我甚至不知道他是怎么给自己做了一根针。
我知道他从他们发的连体服里抽出线来做线，然后他开始裁剪衣服，使它们更合身。

sentences.en: One of my favorite stories was a prisoner who told me that he was in isolation for a number of months, and I'm not even sure how he made himself a needle.
sentences.zh: 他们通常会得到这些非常宽松的连体服，所以他会加上袖口或缩短袖子。

sentences.en: I know that he pulled threads out of the jumpsuits they're given in order to make thread, and then he started tailoring his clothes so that they fit better.
sentences.zh: 我想其他囚犯发现了他在做这件事，在某些情况下，友好的狱警会把制服传过来传过去，

sentences.en: They're often given these very loose jumpsuits, and so he would add cuffs or shorten the sleeves.
sentences.zh: 他开始为其他人裁剪制服。

sentences.en: And I think other prisoners found out about him doing this, and in some cases a friendly officer would pass a uniform back and forth,
sentences.zh: 这有点，并不是说有人在看他们，但这是一种惊人的自我表达和社区感，他们在这个地方设法创造了出来。

sentences.en: and he started tailoring other people's uniforMs.
sentences.zh: 我相信会有很多人说，看，这些单元里有很多人确实是最坏中的最坏。

sentences.en: It's kind of, not that anyone is even seeing them, but it's this amazing kind of self-expression and community that they're managing to create in this place.
sentences.zh: 也许并非所有人都是，但其中一些人可能确实是。

sentences.en: I'm sure there are going to be people who say, look, there are lots of people in these units who really are the worst of the worSt.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人可能确实非常暴力且非常危险，应该待在那里。

sentences.en: Maybe not all of them are, but some of them probably are.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你是否有时觉得他们可能是需要被单独监禁的人？

sentences.en: Some of them probably are really violent and really dangerous and ought to be there.
sentences.zh: 所以隔离室里确实有危险的人。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, do you ever feel that they might be people who need to be in solitary confinement?
sentences.zh: 分析中一个非常重要的点是人们在隔离中度过的时间长度，事实上，我们谈论的不是几周或几个月。

sentences.en: So there are certainly people in isolation who are dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的通常是几年和几十年，而且即使是那些在20多岁时可能相当可怕或危险的人，到了40多岁和50多岁时也不太可能那样了。

sentences.en: One of the really important points of analysis is the length of time people are spending in isolation, the fact that people, we're not talking about weeks or months.
sentences.zh: 当我们审视几十年的这些政策时，我们看到即使是那些被认为最可怕的人，

sentences.en: We're talking about years and decades often, and that even people who might have been fairly scary or dangerous in their 20s are unlikely to be that way into their 40s and 50s.
sentences.zh: 系统在他们身处其中时并没有很好地控制他们。

sentences.en: And as we look at decades of these policies, we see that even some of the people who have been held up as the scariest,
sentences.zh: 而且他们在隔离之外表现得令人惊讶地好。

sentences.en: the system didn't control them very well while they were in it.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实在各个层面上对这种做法提出了质疑。

sentences.en: And they're doing surprisingly well outside of isolation.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实在各个层面上对这种做法提出了质疑。

sentences.en: So it really does call the practice into question on all different levels.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实在各个层面上对这种做法提出了质疑。

sentences.en: So your book comes at a time when many liberals and conservatives have joined hands to call for prison reform.
sentences.zh: 你的书出版之际，正值许多自由派和保守派人士联手呼吁进行监狱改革之时。

sentences.en: For one thing, keeping people in prison and keeping someone in solitary confinement is very, very expensive.
sentences.zh: 首先，将人们关在监狱里，尤其是关在单独监禁中，是非常、非常昂贵的。

sentences.en: Give us a sense of how expensive it is and whether these ideological pairings are triggering any change in the system.
sentences.zh: 请让我们了解一下这到底有多昂贵，以及这种意识形态上的联手是否正在引发体制内的任何变革。

sentences.en: So solitary confinement is astronomically expensive.
sentences.zh: 单独监禁的费用高得惊人。

sentences.en: In states like California, it costs about $45,000 per prisoner per year to keep someone in the general prison population.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州这样的地方，普通监狱中每名囚犯每年的关押成本约为4.5万美元。

sentences.en: And it costs about $90,000 per prisoner per year to keep someone in isolation.
sentences.zh: 而将某人关在隔离区，每名囚犯每年的成本约为9万美元。

sentences.en: So the cost of running the facilities is really expensive because these prisoners in isolation, you know, every need has to be met by someone working in the prison,
sentences.zh: 运营这些设施的成本非常高昂，因为对于这些被隔离的囚犯，你知道，他们的每一项需求都必须由监狱工作人员来满足，

sentences.en: whether it's delivering mail or delivering legal documents or getting them a meal.
sentences.zh: 无论是投递邮件、递送法律文件，还是为他们提供餐食。

sentences.en: And so that's how the costs go up.
sentences.zh: 这就是成本增加的原因。

sentences.en: And the costs of the facilities are also expensive to build these kinds of technologically advanced facilities.
sentences.zh: 而且，建造这类技术先进的设施，其设施本身的造价也很昂贵。

sentences.en: And that's not even wrapped into that per prisoner per year coSt.
sentences.zh: 这甚至还没算进那笔每名囚犯每年的关押成本里。

sentences.en: So I think that has been part of the reform conversation, as you suggest, that perhaps there might be a less expensive way to do this work.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，正如你所言，这已经成为改革讨论的一部分，即或许有成本更低的方式来完成这项工作。

sentences.en: One other cost of isolation is that the vast majority of people, even from long-term solitary confinement, ultimately get out of prison.
sentences.zh: 隔离的另一个代价是，绝大多数人，即使是长期处于单独监禁中的人，最终还是会出狱。

sentences.en: It's 95 to 98 percent of all prisoners get out eventually.
And that's surprisingly true of people in isolation, too.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，对于处于隔离状态的人来说，这也是事实。

sentences.en: And so there's the question of what are the social impacts of letting people out?
sentences.zh: 因此，问题在于，让这些人出狱会带来什么样的社会影响？

sentences.en: And I think in combination, those economic costs and the social costs, people are beginning to think about alternatives.
sentences.zh: 我认为，将这些经济成本和社会成本结合起来看，人们开始考虑替代方案了。

sentences.en: And that is a conversation that crosses political lines.
sentences.zh: 这是一场跨越政治界限的对话。

sentences.en: And prison, as I suggested, in many states, legislators are initiating reforMs.
sentences.zh: 正如我所提到的，在许多州的监狱中，立法者们正在启动改革。

sentences.en: But in many states, prison officials within the system are looking at the norms changing in the critiques of this practice and initiating their own reforms,
sentences.zh: 但在许多州，体制内的监狱官员也在审视这种做法所受到的批评中不断变化的规范，并开始进行他们自己的改革，

sentences.en: saying, what can we do to reduce our reliance on this practice?
sentences.zh: 他们问：我们能做些什么来减少对这种做法的依赖？

sentences.en: Karamit Ryder is a professor at the University of California at Irvine.
sentences.zh: 卡拉米特·莱德是加州大学欧文分校的教授。

sentences.en: She's the author of the book 23-7, Pelican Bay Prison and the Rise of Long-Term Solitary Confinement.
sentences.zh: 她是《23/7：鹈鹕湾监狱与长期单独监禁的兴起》一书的作者。
